description: Customize the collection page (shopify-live-horizon/templates/collection.json) to match the Next.js collection experience while preserving Horizon's native Shopify filtering, sorting, pagination, and collection URLs. Work is primarily editorial header + typography + product-card ratio tuning; the native `filters` block already provides filtering, sorting, grid density, active-filter display, clear-filter controls, product count, and responsive mobile filter UI. Independent of FEAT-001 and FEAT-003 (different template file).
steps: Read context.json first, then read sections/main-collection.liquid, blocks/filters.liquid, snippets/product-grid.liquid, snippets/sorting.liquid, snippets/pagination-controls.liquid, and src/components/collection/CollectionGrid.tsx + src/components/filters/FilterBar.tsx + src/components/product/ProductCard.tsx (READ ONLY) to confirm the target design and the native capabilities already present.

In templates/collection.json, keep the existing `section` header but tune its text blocks: title `

{{ closest.collection.title }}

` to Jost display (font `var(--font-heading--family)`, case none, h1/h2 preset), add a small uppercase eyebrow text block, and keep the rte `{{ closest.collection.description }}` as the editorial description (Inter body).

Keep the `main-collection` `filters` block with enable_filtering/enable_sorting/enable_grid_density true (native active-filter chips, clear-all, product count, and mobile drawer come from blocks/filters.liquid — do not rebuild). Only expose filters backed by real product data (native collection.filters already does this).

Tune the `_product-card` block typography to match ProductCard.tsx: title in Jost, price in Inter with tabular numerals; keep image_ratio `adapt` (or set a consistent portrait ratio) so rug aspect ratios are NOT misleadingly cropped. Keep card badges driven by real product state only.
Preserve pagination/loading: main-collection uses `enable_infinite_scroll` or `products_per_page` — keep Horizon's existing supported behavior; do not hardcode product lists.
Do not invent metafield-backed filters or hardcode products. Preserve working filter/sort query params and collection URLs.
acceptance_criteria: templates/collection.json keeps a `main-collection` section whose static `filters` block has enable_filtering, enable_sorting, and enable_grid_density all true.
Collection header renders Jost h1 title + eyebrow + rte description bound to real `closest.collection.*` objects (no hardcoded title/description).
Product cards show title (Jost), price (Inter), and a non-cropping image ratio; no hardcoded products or invented metafields.
Running `shopify theme check` introduces zero new errors versus baseline.
templates/collection.json is valid JSON after stripping its leading comment banner.

Confirm the `filters` block settings still enable filtering/sorting/grid-density and no product handles are hardcoded in the template.
